title: The value function of a bounded purchase

blocks.text: A regional water utility relines old mains in standard **lots**. Each lot type $`j`$ takes $`a_j`$ crew-days, is worth $`c_j`$ (in $10k of avoided breaks), and can be bought at most $`u_j`$ times this season, because each type needs a liner the supplier rations. With $`d`$ crew-days, the best season is

z(d) \;=\; \max \sum_{j} c_j\, x_j
\qquad \text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{j} a_j\, x_j \le d \quad \text{(days)}, \qquad
x_j \in \{0, 1, \dots, u_j\} \ \ \forall j

Write `value_function(days, worth, limits, capacity)`, which returns the list $`[z(0), z(1), \dots, z(\text{capacity})]`$. `days`, `worth` and `limits` hold $`a_j`$, $`c_j`$ and $`u_j`$ for each lot type, all whole numbers, with every $`a_j \ge 1`$.

A table filled from small $`d`$ to large, as lesson 9.2.1's `value_function` did, works once each type has a limit, if each copy of a type is treated as one more item that can be taken or left. Decide how the table must be updated so that one copy is never counted twice.
The tests compare your list with every purchase enumerated by hand on small instances. About eight lines.

from __future__ import annotations


def value_function(days: list[int], worth: list[int], limits: list[int], capacity: int) -> list[int]:
    """z(d) for d = 0..capacity: the best worth of lots that fit in d crew-days, each type within its limit."""
    z = [0] * (capacity + 1)                     # z[d] = 0: buying nothing always fits
    for a, c, u in zip(days, worth, limits):
        for _ in range(u):                       # each copy of the type is one more item, taken or left
            for d in range(capacity, a - 1, -1):     # downwards, so this copy is used at most once
                z[d] = max(z[d], z[d - a] + c)
    return z


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(value_function([3, 5], [4, 7], [2, 1], 12))

cases.says: z(d) is the best value of any purchase that fits in d, for every d from 0 to the capacity
a type may be bought up to its limit, not just once
a type is never bought more times than its limit allows
a plan need not use the whole capacity, so z never falls as d grows
